t: Authenticator app vs SMS 2FA
k: Authenticator app vs SMS 2FA, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, authenticator app vs sms 2fa
b: Authenticator app vs SMS 2FA An authenticator app is significantly more secure than SMS, because SMS codes can be intercepted through SIM-swap fraud. Use an app wherever you can. How they compare Authenticator app SMS Works without signal Yes No Works abroad / roaming Yes Often unreliable Vulnerable to SIM swap No Yes Vulnerable to carrier delays No Yes Recoverable if you lose the phone Only with backup codes Only with the number What a SIM swap is An attacker persuades your mobile carrier to move your number to a SIM they control — usually with details harvested from a data breach or from you directly. Every SMS code then goes to them. They do not need your phone. This is the single most common way crypto accounts with SMS 2FA are taken over. Good to know Set a port-out PIN / account passcode with your mobile carrier if you must use SMS. An authenticator app generates codes locally on your device. Nothing is transmitted, so nothing can be intercepted. Whichever you use, back it up: save your backup codes and consider pairing a second device. Hardware security keys, where supported, are stronger still. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. No genuine employee will ever ask you to read a code aloud. State your old name and your new name exactly as they appear on the documents. Attach both documents. Submit. You will get a ticket reference. Good to know A simple typo (a misspelling that was never correct) also goes through this process, but only needs your ID. k: How to close your account permanently, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, close account
b: How to close your account permanently Close your account in Settings → Account → Close account . You must sell or withdraw all balances first, and closure is permanent. Before you start Sell or withdraw every asset. An account cannot be closed with a non-zero balance, and small "dust" amounts may need to be swapped or sold first. Export your statements and transaction history. You will need them for tax reporting, and you will not be able to sign in afterwards. Cancel any active savings plans or recurring buys. Steps Open Profile → Settings → Account . Select Close account . Confirm that your balances are zero. The screen lists anything still outstanding. Enter your password and your 2FA code. Choose a reason (optional) and select Close permanently . Confirm the link sent to your registered email. Good to know Closure is irreversible . To return you must register from scratch and verify again. We are legally required to retain certain records — identity documents, transaction history — for a period set by anti-money-laundering law, typically several years. This applies even if you request deletion of your personal data. Any funds arriving after closure will be returned to the sender where possible; on-chain deposits sent to a closed account address may be permanently lost. If you simply want a break, freeze the account instead — that is reversible. Related articles How to freeze (lock) your account How to reactivate a frozen account Was this article helpful? t: How to freeze (lock) your account
k: How to freeze (lock) your account, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, freeze account
b: How to freeze (lock) your account Freezing immediately blocks all logins, trades and withdrawals on your account. Use it the moment you suspect something is wrong. When to freeze You see a login, trade or withdrawal you did not make. You clicked a suspicious link and entered your details. Your phone or laptop has been lost or stolen. You gave someone remote access to your device. Steps If you can sign in: go to Profile → Settings → Security → Freeze account , confirm, and select Freeze now . If you cannot sign in: open the Freeze my account self-service tool at www.betabase.pro (no login required) and confirm via the link sent to your registered email. Email support@www.betabase.pro from your registered address as a backup route, with the subject line Account compromise — freeze . Good to know A freeze takes effect immediately and applies to web and app at once. While frozen: no logins, no trades, no deposits, no withdrawals. Your balances stay exactly as they are. Open orders may be cancelled. Market prices continue to move while frozen — Betabase cannot compensate for price movement during a freeze. Freezing is reversible. See How to reactivate a frozen account . Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. After freezing, change your email password too — that is usually the account the attacker really wants. t: How to reactivate a frozen account
k: How to reactivate a frozen account, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, reactivate frozen account
b: How to reactivate a frozen account Reactivate through the Reactivate account tool at www.betabase.pro or in Settings → Security . If the freeze followed a compromise, expect an identity check first. Before you start Clean up first, or you will simply be re-compromised: Change your Betabase password and your email password. Re-pair 2FA on a device you trust and generate fresh backup codes. Run a malware scan on any device you signed in from. Remove any browser extension or remote-access app you did not install yourself. Steps Go to www.betabase.pro and open the Reactivate account tool, or sign in and open Settings → Security → Reactivate . Confirm your identity — normally an email link plus a 2FA code, or a liveness check if the freeze was triggered by suspected fraud. Review the list of active sessions and payout addresses and revoke anything you do not recognise. Confirm reactivation. Good to know Self-service freezes usually lift within minutes once identity is confirmed. Freezes applied by Betabase for compliance or fraud reasons are lifted only after review, which can take several business days. Withdrawals stay locked for a cooling-off period (commonly 24–72 hours) after reactivation. Trading normally resumes at once. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. Nobody can reactivate your account "for a fee" — those offers are scams. t: How to reset 2FA when you lose your device
k: How to reset 2FA when you lose your device, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, reset 2fa lost device
b: How to reset 2FA when you lose your device If you still have a backup code, use it to sign in and re-pair 2FA yourself. If you have no backup codes, request a 2FA reset — this requires an identity check. Option 1 — you have a backup code (fastest) On the login screen, enter your email and password. At the 2FA prompt, select Use a backup code . Enter one unused backup code. Each code works once. Once in, go to Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication → Reset and pair your new device. Generate a fresh set of backup codes — the old set is now void. Option 2 — no backup codes (identity check required) On the login screen, select Can't access your 2FA? — or open the Reset 2FA tool at www.betabase.pro. Confirm your email address. We send you a link. Complete a liveness check : a short video selfie plus your photo ID, so we can confirm you are the account holder. Submit the request and wait. This is a manual review. Good to know A 2FA reset typically takes 1–3 business days. It cannot be rushed — the delay is the security. Withdrawals are locked for a cooling-off period (commonly 24–72 hours) after a 2FA reset. This is deliberate and protects you if an attacker were attempting the reset. Your funds are safe while you wait. Nobody can withdraw without the new 2FA. Support cannot bypass 2FA, no matter how urgent the situation is. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. "Fast 2FA reset" services on social media are scams, without exception. b: How to set up two-factor authentication (2FA) Set up 2FA in Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication : scan a QR code with an authenticator app, confirm a code, and save your backup codes. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app. If you cannot scan, copy the setup key manually. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows to confirm the pairing. Save your backup codes. Write them down on paper or store them in a password manager — not as a screenshot in your phone gallery. Select Activate . 2FA is now required at login and for sensitive actions. Good to know 2FA is required for withdrawals, password changes, email changes and adding payout addresses. Codes rotate every 30 seconds. If codes are rejected, check that your phone's clock is set to automatic time. You can pair the same account with more than one device — a spare phone or tablet is a cheap insurance policy. t: How to spot phishing and fake support
k: How to spot phishing and fake support, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, spot phishing fake support
b: How to spot phishing and fake support Phishing tries to get you to hand over your password, 2FA code or crypto by pretending to be Betabase. The single best defence is to never act on an incoming message. The rules that keep you safe Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. No exceptions, no emergencies, no "verification checks". We never ask you to install remote-access or screen-sharing software. We never DM you first on Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, X or Instagram. Every "support agent" who contacts you there is a fraudster. We never ask you to move funds to a "safe wallet", "vault" or "recovery address". That is theft, described in reassuring language. We never phone you to ask you to approve a withdrawal. Red flags Urgency and threats: "your account will be closed in 24 hours". A link whose domain is nearly, but not exactly, www.betabase.pro — extra hyphens, a different ending, a lookalike character. Unexpected attachments, or a login page reached from an email rather than typed by you. Anyone offering to "recover" funds you already lost, for an upfront fee. That is a second scam targeting victims of the first. What to do if you clicked Freeze your account immediately. Change your Betabase password and your email password. Reset 2FA and revoke unknown sessions and devices. Report it to support@www.betabase.pro with screenshots. On-chain transfers cannot be reversed. If you send crypto to a scammer, Betabase cannot get it back. Related articles How to freeze (lock) your account Authenticator app vs SMS 2FA What is a wallet, and who holds my coins? b: How to update your residential address Update your address in Settings → Personal details → Address . Most changes require a fresh proof-of-address document. Before you start Prepare a document dated within the last 3 months showing your full name and the new address: a utility bill (gas, electricity, water, landline — not mobile); a bank or credit-card statement; a council tax, tax authority or other government letter; a residence certificate. The file must be a full-page, unedited colour scan or photo. All four corners must be visible. Steps Open Profile → Settings → Personal details . Next to Address , select Change . Enter the new address exactly as it appears on your document. Upload your proof of address. Select Submit . The status shows In review . Good to know Review usually completes within 1–3 business days. You get an email either way. Documents are rejected if they are cropped, blurred, expired, screenshotted from a banking app without the name and date visible, or in a different name. If you have moved to a country Betabase does not serve, your account will move to withdrawal-only. You will be able to sell and withdraw, but not deposit or buy. k: I cannot log in to my account (troubleshooting), Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, cannot log in
b: I cannot log in to my account (troubleshooting) Work through the cause: wrong credentials, a 2FA code problem, an undelivered email or SMS, or a temporary lock after too many failed attempts. 1. "Invalid email or password" Check for a stray space, a capital letter, or the wrong keyboard layout. Make sure you are using the email you actually registered with — try any alternatives you own. Still stuck? Use Forgot password? to reset. 2. Your 2FA code is rejected Codes rotate every 30 seconds. Wait for a fresh one and type it quickly. Set your phone's date and time to automatic . A clock that has drifted is by far the most common cause of "invalid code". Confirm you are reading the code for the right account inside your authenticator app. No device? See How to reset 2FA when you lose your device . 3. No email or SMS arriving Check spam and promotions folders; whitelist our sending domain. SMS: check signal, disable any call/SMS blocker, and note that roaming can block delivery. Wait 5 minutes before requesting a resend — rapid resends can queue behind each other. 4. "Too many attempts" / temporarily locked Failed logins trigger a temporary lock. Wait 30 minutes and try again — do not keep retrying, that extends the lock. Good to know If none of this works, or you see activity you do not recognise, freeze the account and contact support@www.betabase.pro. Support is available 24/7. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. Support will never ask you to log in on their behalf. t: What are backup codes and how to use them
k: What are backup codes and how to use them, Account & security, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, backup codes
b: What are backup codes and how to use them Backup codes are one-time codes that let you log in when your 2FA device is unavailable. You get them when you switch 2FA on — save them then. How to use one Sign in with your email and password. At the 2FA prompt, select Use a backup code . Enter one unused code. It is consumed immediately and cannot be reused. Once inside, go to Settings → Security and re-pair 2FA on your new device. Where to find or regenerate them Open Profile → Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication . Select Backup codes → Generate new codes . Confirm with your password and a current 2FA code. Store the new set. Generating a new set invalidates every previous code. How to store them Print them, or write them out, and keep them somewhere physically secure — a safe, a locked drawer, with important documents. Or store them in a reputable password manager. Do not keep them in your phone's photo gallery, in a plain text file on your desktop, in your email, or in cloud notes. Those are exactly the places an attacker looks first. Good to know Each code works once. When you have used most of them, regenerate the set. Backup codes are the only way to get back in without a manual 2FA reset, which takes days. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. Anyone who has your backup codes can take your account — treat them like cash. b: How to buy cryptocurrency You buy crypto by opening Trade → Buy , selecting an asset, entering an amount of EUR to spend, reviewing the quote and confirming the order. Before you start Verification must be complete and you need a settled cash balance . Pending deposits cannot be spent. Check the minimum trade amount for that asset (see Minimum trade amounts ). Steps From the dashboard, select Trade (or Buy in the Betabase app). Search for the asset and select it. Select the Buy tab. Enter the amount you want to spend in EUR. You can also toggle the input to enter a quantity of the asset instead. Fractions are fine — you never need to buy a whole coin. Choose your order type: Market (executes now at the best available price) or Limit (executes only at your price or better). Review the summary: estimated quantity received, price, spread and fee. Select Confirm . The order appears immediately under Transactions . Good to know Market orders fill in seconds. Limit orders sit open until the market reaches your price, or until you cancel them. The quote you see is indicative and time-limited. If it expires, refresh it — the market has moved. Your cash is reserved the moment you place a limit order, so it cannot be spent twice. Crypto is volatile and your capital is at risk. You may get back less than you put in. Nothing here is investment advice, and Betabase never recommends specific assets. k: How to cancel or edit an open order, Buying, selling & swapping, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, cancel or edit open order
b: How to cancel or edit an open order You can cancel any order that has not yet filled from Transactions → Open orders . To change a price or amount, you cancel the order and place a new one. Steps Go to Transactions → Open orders (or Orders in the Betabase app). Find the order. Check its status is Open , Pending or Pending trigger . Select the order to open its detail view. Select Cancel order and confirm. The status changes to Cancelled and any reserved cash or crypto returns to your available balance. Good to know Most platforms do not support in-place editing of a live order. Cancel and replace is the standard method — and it is what the Edit button does behind the scenes where it exists. A market order cannot be cancelled. It executes in a fraction of a second; by the time you can tap anything, it has filled. Cancelling a partially filled order cancels only the unfilled remainder. The filled part is yours and stays. There is no fee to cancel or place an order. Fees are charged only on execution. If a cancel request arrives at the same moment the order fills, the fill wins. You will see Filled , not Cancelled , and that is final. Cancelling and replacing means losing your place in the queue. In a fast market the new order may fill at a very different price. b: Market orders vs limit orders explained A market order prioritises speed and fills immediately at the best available price. You control the amount , not the price . The final price can differ slightly from the quote you saw (see Why the price I got differs from the price I saw ). Best when you want certainty that the order will happen. Limit orders You set a price. A buy limit fills at your price or lower; a sell limit fills at your price or higher. You control the price , not whether it fills . If the market never reaches your price, the order simply stays open — potentially forever. Your cash (for a buy) or crypto (for a sell) is reserved while the order is open, so you cannot spend it elsewhere. Large limit orders may fill in pieces (see Order status ). Good to know A limit order set far from the current price can sit open for weeks. Set an expiry ( Good til cancelled , Good for day ) if your platform region offers one. In a fast-moving market a limit order can be skipped entirely if the price gaps straight through your level. Neither order type protects you from loss. b: Order status: pending, filled, partially filled, cancelled Every order carries a status that tells you exactly where it is. You'll find it under Transactions → Orders . You already own the filled part, and the remaining amount stays reserved. Cancelling now keeps the filled part and releases the rest. Filled. Fully executed. b: Understanding your portfolio, average buy price and total return Your average buy price is the weighted average of everything you paid for an asset, and your total return compares that against its current value. How the numbers work Average buy price = total EUR spent on that asset (including fees, where shown) ÷ total quantity held. Every new buy pulls the average towards the price you just paid. Unrealised return = current value − (average buy price × quantity held). It changes every second with the market and only becomes real when you sell. Realised return = the profit or loss on units you have already sold. Total return combines the two, and where relevant includes rewards received. Selling part of a holding does not change your average buy price — it reduces the quantity, not the cost per unit. Good to know Percentage figures on the dashboard show the market's move over a selected time range. The figure on the asset page shows your return. They will differ, and that is expected. Crypto received from staking rewards or promotions may enter at a cost basis of zero, which lowers your average. Values shown in a display currency other than EUR use an indicative FX rate and are rounded. These figures are indicative and are not a tax calculation. For tax, export your full transaction history. It is a real cost, and it is why a coin you buy and instantly sell shows a small loss. Slippage. Between you tapping Confirm and the order executing, the market moves. In volatile conditions or on thinly traded assets, that move can be meaningful. Larger orders can also consume several price levels, so the average fill price is worse than the top price. Quote expiry. Quotes are valid for a few seconds. Let one lapse and the refreshed quote reflects a new market. To control the price rather than the timing, use a limit order — it will not fill above (buy) or below (sell) your chosen level. b: How long do crypto deposits take? (confirmations explained) A crypto deposit credits once it has enough confirmations on its network — usually minutes, occasionally an hour or more when the network is busy. What a confirmation is When you send crypto, the transaction waits in a queue (the mempool) until a validator packs it into a block . That is confirmation one. Every block built on top of it adds another confirmation, making the transaction progressively harder to undo. Betabase waits for a set number of confirmations per asset before crediting your balance — a slow, heavy network needs fewer; a fast, light one needs more. Steps to track a pending deposit Open Transactions in Betabase. The deposit appears with a Pending status and a confirmation count. Copy the transaction hash (TXID) from your sending wallet. Paste it into a public block explorer for that network. Read the status: - Not found — the transfer never left your wallet. The problem is on the sending side. - Pending / unconfirmed — it is in the queue. Wait. A low network fee means a longer wait. - Confirmed — it is on-chain, and Betabase will credit it once the required confirmation count is reached. Good to know Crypto networks run 24/7 — weekends and holidays make no difference. A transaction sent with too low a network fee can sit unconfirmed for hours. Only the sender's wallet can attempt to speed it up (via RBF or a child-pays-for-parent transaction), never Betabase. Confirmed on-chain but not credited after several hours? Contact support@www.betabase.pro with the TXID, asset, network and amount. Support is available 24/7. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. Once broadcast, a transfer cannot be cancelled or recalled by you or by Betabase. t: I sent crypto on the wrong network — what happens now?
k: I sent crypto on the wrong network — what happens now?, Deposits & funding, width=device-width,initial-scale=1, sent crypto wrong network
b: I sent crypto on the wrong network — what happens now? It depends entirely on which network you used — some wrong-network deposits can be recovered manually, and some are permanently and unrecoverably lost. The honest answer Blockchain transactions are irreversible. Once a transfer is confirmed, it cannot be cancelled, reversed or recalled — not by you, not by Betabase, not by anyone. What matters now is whether Betabase happens to control the private key for the address you sent to, on the network you used. Sometimes recoverable. If you sent an asset on a network Betabase supports, to an address we control on that network — for example a token sent to an EVM address that is valid on several EVM chains — a manual recovery may be possible. It is a slow, engineering-led process, may carry a recovery fee, and is never guaranteed . Not recoverable. If you sent to a network Betabase does not support at all, or to an address type nobody holds the key for, the funds are gone. No support ticket, tool or paid "recovery service" can bring them back. Steps Stop. Do not send anything else to the same address. Find the transaction hash (TXID) in your sending wallet. Confirm on a block explorer which network it actually went out on, and that it is confirmed. Contact support@www.betabase.pro with: the TXID, the exact asset and token contract, the network used, the intended network, the destination address, the amount and the date. Wait for the assessment. Do not open duplicate tickets — it slows the queue, not speeds it. How to never do this again Always select the network in Betabase first , then match it in the sending wallet. Always send a small test amount before a large transfer. Copy addresses with the copy button. Verify the first and last four characters. Anyone contacting you offering to "recover" lost crypto for an upfront fee is a scammer, without exception. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. b: Understanding deposit addresses and networks (choosing the right chain) A deposit address only works for the specific asset and the specific network it was generated for — choosing the wrong network is the most common way people lose crypto. Why networks matter The same token often exists on several blockchains at once. USDT, for example, runs on Ethereum ( ERC-20 ), Tron ( TRC-20 ), BNB Chain ( BEP-20 ), Solana and others. They share a name and a price, but they are separate assets on separate ledgers that cannot see each other. An ERC-20 address and a TRC-20 address are not interchangeable, even when they look similar. How to choose In Betabase, open Deposit → Crypto and select your asset. The supported networks are listed. Open your sending wallet or exchange and look at which networks it offers for the withdrawal. Pick a network that appears on both lists. Set that network on the sending side before you paste the address. Compare the first four and last four characters of the pasted address against the original. Address-swapping malware exists. Send a small test amount first, wait for it to arrive, then send the rest. Good to know Networks differ in cost and speed. Ethereum is often the most expensive; alternatives are usually cheaper and faster. If both sides support several, the cheaper one is fine. Ethereum-style addresses (starting 0x ) look identical across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon and others — the address format tells you nothing about which chain is correct. Layer-2 networks (for example Arbitrum, Optimism, Base) are separate networks too, even though they use 0x addresses. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. Sending on an unsupported network usually means permanent loss, and there is no undo — not by you, not by Betabase, not by anyone. b: What is a memo / destination tag and when do I need one? A memo (or destination tag) is a short code that tells Betabase which customer a deposit belongs to, because some networks route every user's funds through one shared address. Which assets need one Networks that use a shared deposit address require a memo or tag. These commonly include XRP (destination tag), XLM (memo), EOS, ATOM, HBAR, ALGO and some others. The deposit screen tells you plainly: if a memo field is shown, it is mandatory . Steps Open Deposit → Crypto and select the asset and network. If a memo/tag is required, Betabase shows it below the address, clearly labelled. Copy the address into the address field of your sending wallet. Copy the memo/tag into the wallet's memo, tag, note or reference field. It is a separate field — never paste it into the address. Check both against the original before you send. Send. Good to know The memo is not optional and it is not a personal note. It is the only thing that identifies you inside a shared address. Some wallets label the field differently: Memo , Tag , Destination tag , Note , Comment . If in doubt, look for the field that appears only for that specific coin. If your wallet has no memo field, it probably cannot send that asset correctly. Use a wallet that does. A deposit sent without a required memo, or with the wrong memo, does not credit automatically. Recovery is sometimes possible but is manual, slow, may carry a fee, and is not guaranteed . Contact support@www.betabase.pro with the transaction hash, the amount and the date. Blockchain transactions are irreversible — we cannot reverse the transfer, only attempt to identify it. b: Why must the bank account be in my own name? (third-party payment rule) Money can only enter or leave your Betabase account through a bank account or card held in your own name — this is a legal anti-money-laundering requirement, not a policy we can waive. Why the rule exists AML regulation requires a regulated firm to know that the person who owns the account is the person whose money is moving through it. If we accepted payments from other people, Betabase would have no way to know whose funds those really are — which is exactly the gap money laundering exploits. Every regulated exchange and broker applies the same rule. What happens to a third-party payment The payment is detected as coming from a name that does not match your account. It is not credited to your balance. It is quarantined and returned to the sending account. This typically takes 5–10 business days . Your bank, and any intermediary bank, may deduct a return fee. You may get back less than you sent. Repeated third-party payments can get the account restricted. Good to know Joint accounts are usually accepted if you are one of the named holders — check with support at support@www.betabase.pro before sending. Business accounts must be funded from a corporate account in the company's name, never from a director's personal account. Name variations matter: "Rob Smith" versus "Robert Smith" can trigger a hold. Match your ID exactly. If you have recently changed your legal name, update Profile → Personal details and supply the change-of-name document before you deposit. If anyone asks you to receive money into your bank account and forward it as crypto, that is money muling — a criminal offence, and the account will be closed and reported. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. b: Betabase fee overview Betabase charges in four places: on trades, on some deposits, on some withdrawals, and on network transfers. Everything is published on the Fees & limits page at www.betabase.pro, and shown to you before you confirm. The four categories Trading fees. Charged when an order executes. Depending on your region and asset, this is a spread built into the price, an explicit commission , or both. Nothing is charged on an order that does not fill. Deposit fees. Standard bank transfers are commonly free. Cards and some instant methods carry a percentage fee because the payment provider charges one. Withdrawal fees. EUR withdrawals to your bank may carry a flat fee. Crypto withdrawals carry a network fee , which is paid to the blockchain, not to Betabase. Other fees. Some regions apply an inactivity fee after a long dormant period, or fees for premium products. These are always listed in the fee schedule. Good to know The full cost of any transaction is shown in the confirmation summary before you commit. Betabase does not add charges after execution. Fees can differ by country, asset, payment method and verification tier. The fee schedule is the authoritative source; this article is a summary. Fees may change. Material changes are announced in advance in line with the Terms of Service. Third parties may charge you separately — your bank, your card issuer (which may treat a crypto purchase as a cash advance) or a foreign-exchange conversion. b: Daily and monthly transaction limits Limits apply per rolling window — usually 24 hours, 30 days and sometimes 12 months — and are counted separately for deposits, withdrawals and, in some regions, trading. How the windows work A rolling 24-hour window counts everything in the last 24 hours from right now . It does not reset at midnight. A withdrawal made at 3pm yesterday frees up its allowance at 3pm today. The 30-day window works the same way. Because they roll, capacity returns gradually rather than all at once. What counts toward what Deposit limits count money coming in, per method. Cards often have a lower cap than bank transfers. Withdrawal limits count EUR and crypto separately in most regions. Crypto limits are usually expressed as a EUR-equivalent value at the time of the withdrawal. Trading limits , where they exist, count executed order value. Cancelled orders do not count. Reserved funds on an open order do not consume a limit until the order actually fills. If you hit a limit Check Profile → Limits to see exactly which limit is exhausted and when capacity returns. Wait for the window to roll, or Apply for a higher tier under Increase my limits . Good to know Limits may be tightened temporarily during a security review of your account. Payment providers and your own bank apply their own separate caps, which Betabase cannot change. b: Why network fees change (gas / congestion) Network fees change because block space is scarce and priced by demand. When more people want their transaction in the next block than there is room for, they bid the fee up. How it works A blockchain fits only a limited amount of data into each block, and blocks arrive at a fixed rate. Pending transactions wait in the mempool . Validators pick the most profitable ones first. To go first, you attach a higher fee. This bidding is what "gas" prices on Ethereum-style chains describe. When demand falls, so does the price — which is why the same withdrawal can cost a fraction of yesterday's fee. What drives spikes A market-wide surge in trading, a popular launch, or a liquidation cascade. Bots competing for the same block. Complex transactions consuming more block space than a simple transfer. How to pay less Withdraw once for a larger amount rather than several times for small ones — the fee is per transaction, not per coin. Where the asset supports more than one network, compare the fee for each before you choose. But only pick a network your destination wallet or exchange actually supports. Send at quieter times. Fees are often lower outside peak trading hours. Good to know Betabase passes the network fee through and does not profit from it. The fee estimate shown is exactly that — an estimate at the moment you look. Choosing the wrong network to save on fees is the most expensive mistake in crypto. Funds sent over an unsupported network are usually unrecoverable. Related articles Withdrawal and network fees explained What is a blockchain? Betabase fee overview Was this article helpful? b: What is a blockchain? A blockchain is a shared record of transactions, grouped into blocks and chained together so that changing an old entry would mean redoing everything after it. How it works You send a transaction. It goes into a waiting area called the mempool. A validator (a miner or staker, depending on the network) picks transactions and packs them into a block . The block is broadcast and every node checks it against the network's rules. Each new block built on top of yours is one more confirmation . More confirmations means the transaction is harder to undo. Most platforms wait for a set number of confirmations before crediting funds. Why it matters to you Transfers are final. Once confirmed, an on-chain transaction cannot be cancelled, reversed or recalled — not by you, not by Betabase, not by anyone. Sending to a wrong address usually means the funds are gone. Networks are separate. The same-looking address on two different networks is not interchangeable. Sending an asset over the wrong network can cause permanent loss. Fees vary. Network fees are set by network demand, not by Betabase. They rise when the network is busy. Speed varies. Confirmation times range from seconds to over an hour depending on the network and congestion. Always check the address and the network twice before you confirm any on-chain withdrawal. b: What is cryptocurrency? A cryptocurrency is a digital asset whose ownership is recorded on a shared public ledger — a blockchain — rather than by a single bank or government. The short version Traditional money exists as an entry in your bank's private database. Your bank alone decides what that database says. A cryptocurrency instead records balances on a ledger that thousands of independent computers hold a copy of, and they agree on updates using cryptography and a set of shared rules. No single party can quietly rewrite it. Key ideas Decentralised. No central issuer or administrator for most major coins. Scarce by design. Many coins have a fixed or predictable supply written into their code. Scarcity does not guarantee value. Divisible. You can own a tiny fraction of a coin. You never have to buy a whole one. Coins vs tokens. A coin is native to its own blockchain. A token is issued on top of someone else's blockchain. Pseudonymous, not anonymous. Transactions are public; addresses are not directly linked to names, but they can often be traced. Good to know Crypto is not legal tender in most countries, is not covered by deposit-guarantee schemes, and carries no interest by default. b: Tax Security Deposit – Frequently Asked Questions A Tax Security Deposit is a temporary, separate security amount used only to complete verification before funds can be released. It is not a tax, not a fee, and not a service charge. Betabase is not a tax authority and does not independently determine a client’s personal tax liability. This article is general information, not tax advice. Any tax liability is determined in accordance with applicable law and the client’s individual circumstances. When may tax requirements affect the release of funds? The release of funds may be subject to applicable tax, regulatory, compliance, and verification requirements relating to the transaction or the client, depending on the applicable law and circumstances. Where a temporary security mechanism is required to complete the relevant verification process, the client may be required to provide a Tax Security Deposit in accordance with the applicable procedure and the terms communicated to the client. Important: The Company is not a tax authority and does not independently determine a client’s personal tax liability. Any tax liability is determined in accordance with applicable law and the client’s individual circumstances. What is a Tax Security Deposit? A Tax Security Deposit is a temporary security deposit intended to secure the completion of the required verification and review process before the release of funds. The deposit is held temporarily for this purpose only. The Tax Security Deposit is not a tax payment, is not a fee, is not a service charge, and does not constitute revenue of the Company. Is the Tax Security Deposit a tax payment? No. The Tax Security Deposit does not constitute a payment of tax to a tax authority and does not replace or settle any tax liability that may apply to the client. Where a client has a tax liability under applicable law, that liability must be addressed in accordance with the requirements of the relevant law and competent tax authority. The Tax Security Deposit is a separate security mechanism used solely for the completion of the applicable verification procedure. Why can’t the Tax Security Deposit simply be deducted from the funds already held in my account? The Tax Security Deposit is required as a separate security amount from the existing account balance. Depending on the applicable regulatory, contractual, and administrative requirements governing the handling of client funds, the deposit cannot be automatically offset against or deducted from the balance designated for release. Accordingly, where a security deposit is required, it must be provided separately from the existing funds, in accordance with the applicable procedure communicated to the client. The existing balance does not become the security deposit and cannot be used as a substitute for the required security amount. How long is the Tax Security Deposit held? The Tax Security Deposit is held on a temporary basis only. The security period is up to 7 business days , subject to completion of the required verification and review procedures. Where the applicable process is completed earlier, the procedure may be finalized before the end of the seven-business-day period. Will the Tax Security Deposit be refunded? Yes. Once the required verification process has been completed and the applicable release conditions have been satisfied, the Tax Security Deposit will be released and returned to the client in full , in accordance with the applicable procedure. The deposit is not intended to constitute income, a fee, or a payment to the Company. Can the Company use the Tax Security Deposit to pay my taxes? No. The Tax Security Deposit does not constitute a tax payment and is not intended to be used to pay a tax authority on behalf of the client, unless an express legal requirement and an applicable mechanism provide otherwise. The client remains responsible for any personal tax obligations applicable to them. The Company does not act as the client’s personal tax adviser. What happens after the Tax Security Deposit is provided? Once the deposit has been received, the Company may proceed with the required verification and review process. Following successful completion of the verification process, and provided that there is no other legal, regulatory, or operational restriction, the withdrawal or release request may proceed to the next administrative stage in accordance with the Company’s procedures. The Tax Security Deposit will be handled in accordance with the applicable terms and will be returned in full once the relevant release conditions have been satisfied. Is there any fee or deduction from the Tax Security Deposit? No. The Tax Security Deposit is not a fee, processing charge, or service charge. Subject to any mandatory legal requirement that may apply, the amount returned to the client will be 100% of the Tax Security Deposit provided, without deduction. Does the Tax Security Deposit reduce the amount of funds I am due to receive? No. The Tax Security Deposit is a separate amount from the existing account balance and from the funds designated for release. Once the applicable procedure has been completed, the Tax Security Deposit and the funds eligible for release will be handled in accordance with the applicable release conditions. What should I do if I am unsure whether the request is legitimate? Any request for a Tax Security Deposit should be received through an official Company communication channel and should be capable of being independently verified. The Company will never ask a client to provide passwords, 2FA codes, private keys, or recovery/seed phrases. If you have any doubt regarding a request, contact the Company through its official support channel before taking any action. b: How to pause, edit or delete a savings plan You can pause, edit or delete any plan at any time from Savings plans . Changes take effect from the next execution, never retroactively. Steps Open Savings plans and select the plan you want to change. Select Manage , then choose: - Pause — the plan stops running but keeps all its settings. Resume it whenever you like. - Edit — change the amount, frequency, execution day, asset split or funding source. - Delete — remove the plan permanently. Confirm. The plan's status and next execution date update immediately. Good to know Your existing crypto is not affected. Pausing or deleting a plan stops future buys only. Everything already purchased stays in your portfolio until you choose to sell it. Changes made very close to an execution time may not apply to that run — the instalment may already be in flight. Cancel at least a day ahead to be certain. Pausing does not cancel a direct debit at your bank; it simply stops Betabase collecting. If you want the mandate gone entirely, delete the plan. There is no fee to pause, edit or delete a plan. A deleted plan cannot be restored. Its history remains under Transactions , but you would need to create a new plan from scratch. Do not cancel a direct debit at your bank without first pausing or deleting the plan on Betabase. A failed collection can leave your account short and may incur a charge from your bank. b: Risks of Earn products (capital at risk, no guaranteed yield) Earn and staking products are not savings accounts . They pay variable rewards in a volatile asset, they lock your funds, and you can lose money — including everything you put in. The risks in full Price risk — the big one. Rewards are paid in the asset you staked. If that asset's price falls, the value of your holding falls with it, and any reward can be wiped out many times over. A positive reward rate and a negative outcome are entirely compatible. No guaranteed yield. Rates are set by the network and vary continuously. They can fall, and in some conditions they can be zero. Any rate shown anywhere on Betabase is an estimate based on recent conditions, never a promise or an offer. Lock-up and illiquidity. Staked assets cannot be sold, swapped or withdrawn until unstaked, and unbonding takes time. You may be unable to exit precisely when you most want to. Slashing. Proof-of-stake networks penalise validators that misbehave or go offline by destroying part of the stake. Where a network applies slashing, some or all of a staked balance can be lost. Protocol and technical risk. Bugs, network upgrades, forks and halts can affect rewards or access to assets. No protection scheme. Crypto held on any platform is generally not covered by deposit-guarantee or investor-compensation schemes the way bank cash is. Regulatory and tax risk. Availability can change, and rewards are usually taxable income in your country. Your capital is at risk. You may lose some or all of it. Earn products are not deposits, not savings, not interest and not investment advice. Never commit money you cannot afford to lose, and be deeply sceptical of any product — anywhere — that advertises a guaranteed or fixed crypto return. Guaranteed returns are a hallmark of fraud. b: Staking rewards, lock-up periods and unstaking Rewards accrue while your assets are staked and are paid out on the network's own schedule. Unstaking is not instant — most networks impose an unbonding period before you get your assets back. Rewards Rewards are paid in the staked asset , not in EUR. The rate is variable and set by the network, not by Betabase. It changes as network participation changes. Any figure shown in the app is an estimate based on recent conditions, not a promise. Payout frequency varies by network — daily, per epoch, or per era. Some networks have a warm-up period before the first reward arrives. Any service fee is deducted before the reward is credited and is disclosed in the fee schedule. Lock-up and unstaking Select the staked asset and choose Unstake . Enter the amount and confirm. The asset enters an unbonding period set by the network — this can range from a few hours to several weeks depending on the chain. During unbonding you earn no rewards and cannot sell, swap or withdraw the asset. When the period ends, the balance returns to your available portfolio automatically. Good to know Betabase cannot shorten or waive an unbonding period. It is a rule of the blockchain. The price can move a long way while you are locked up. This is the central risk of staking. Your capital is at risk. You cannot exit a staked position during the lock-up or unbonding period, even in a sharp market fall. Rewards are variable, may be reduced, and are never guaranteed. b: What is a savings plan (recurring buy / DCA)? A savings plan is a standing instruction to buy a fixed amount of an asset on a repeating schedule — weekly, fortnightly or monthly — without you placing each order by hand. How it works You choose an asset, an instalment amount in EUR, a frequency and a funding source. On each execution date, Betabase places a buy order for that amount automatically. The crypto lands in your portfolio and the plan waits for the next date. Cost averaging, explained honestly Because the instalment is a fixed EUR amount, you automatically buy a smaller quantity when the price is high and a larger quantity when it is low. Over many instalments this produces an average entry price rather than a single one, which removes the need to pick a moment to buy. That is the mechanic — and that is all it is. It is not a strategy that produces profit, and it does not protect you from loss. If the asset's price falls over the life of your plan, cost averaging simply means you bought the fall in pieces. You can still lose money, including all of it. Good to know Each instalment is a normal trade and is subject to the usual spread and fee. Instalments have their own minimum, which may differ from the one-off trade minimum. You can run several plans across different assets at once. A savings plan does not guarantee any return, and it is not investment advice. Crypto is volatile and your capital is at risk — you may get back less than you put in. b: What is staking and how does it work on Betabase? Staking means committing crypto to help secure a proof-of-stake blockchain. In return, the network may pay rewards in that same asset. On Betabase, eligible assets can be staked from your portfolio without you running a validator yourself. How it works A proof-of-stake network needs participants to lock up coins as collateral and validate transactions. The network issues rewards to those validators, and penalises dishonest or offline ones. Betabase pools eligible balances and stakes them with validators on your behalf. Any reward received, less any service fee disclosed in the fee schedule, is credited to you. Steps Open the asset in Portfolio . If staking is offered in your country, you'll see a Stake option. Read the product terms in full, including the lock-up and unstaking periods. Enter the amount to stake and confirm. The staked balance is shown separately in your portfolio. Rewards appear under Transactions as they are received. Good to know Rewards are variable . They depend on network conditions, validator performance and the total amount staked network-wide. They are not interest, not a deposit and not a fixed yield. Staked assets are usually locked and cannot be sold, swapped or withdrawn until unstaked. Not all assets or all countries support staking. Your capital is at risk. Staking does not protect the value of your holding — the asset's price can fall by more than any reward. Rewards are variable and never guaranteed, and in some cases can be zero. This is not investment advice. b: Why a savings plan execution failed A skipped instalment almost always comes down to money, limits or the asset itself. The exact reason is shown on the plan's detail page. The common causes Insufficient cash balance. For plans funded from your Betabase balance, the full instalment plus fee must be available on the execution date. Reserved funds on open orders do not count. The direct debit or card payment was declined. Your bank returned it — insufficient funds, an expired card, a cancelled mandate, or the bank's own fraud block. Fix it with your bank first, then update the funding source on Betabase. A limit was reached. A daily or monthly limit, or your verification tier's cap, blocked the buy. Check Profile → Limits . The asset is suspended. Trading may be paused for a network upgrade, a listing review or extreme volatility. The instalment is skipped for that asset only. Verification lapsed. An expired ID document puts the account into a restricted state, which stops plans. What happens next You are notified by email and in-app. The plan is not deleted. It stays active and tries again on the next scheduled date. Missed instalments are not automatically caught up. If you want the missed amount invested, place a one-off buy manually. After several consecutive failures the plan may be paused automatically. Resume it under Savings plans → Manage once the cause is fixed. b: A deposit is taking longer than expected Card and instant payments usually credit within minutes; standard bank transfers typically take 1–2 business days; crypto arrives after the network reaches the required confirmations. Before you start Check what actually applies to your deposit: Bank transfer: 1–2 business days. Nothing moves at weekends or on bank holidays. A payment sent Friday evening may not settle until Tuesday. Card / instant payment: minutes, occasionally up to an hour. Crypto: minutes to over an hour, depending on the network, its congestion, and the fee the sender paid. Steps Confirm the money actually left the sender: check your bank statement or, for crypto, look up the transaction hash on a block explorer. For bank transfers, check you included the reference code exactly as shown. A missing, edited or truncated reference is the single most common cause of a delayed deposit — it must be matched manually. Confirm the sending account is in your own name . Third-party payments are rejected and returned, which takes days and may cost a fee. For crypto, confirm you used the correct network and the exact deposit address from your logged-in account. Wait out the normal window above before contacting support. If it's outside the window, contact support with the amount, date, sending account and the reference or transaction hash. Good to know Larger or first-time deposits may be held briefly for routine compliance checks. This is normal and not a sign of a problem. Network fees are set by the blockchain, not by Betabase. A low fee paid by the sender means a slow confirmation. Only ever send money to the account details or deposit address shown inside your logged-in account . b: A withdrawal is stuck as pending A pending withdrawal is normally waiting on one of three things: your own email/2FA confirmation, a routine security hold, or blockchain/banking settlement. Steps Check your email. Many withdrawals require you to confirm the request from a link . Until you click it, nothing is sent. Check spam. Open Transactions and select the withdrawal to see its exact status. If the status shows a security hold , this is standard — new withdrawal addresses, new devices and unusually large amounts trigger a cooling-off period, typically up to 24–48 hours. It exists to protect you if your account is ever compromised. If the status shows sent or broadcast and gives a transaction hash, Betabase's part is finished. Paste the hash into a block explorer to see where it is on the network. A low network fee during congestion means a slow confirmation. For a cash withdrawal shown as sent, allow 1–2 business days for your bank to post it. Banks do not settle at weekends. If it is outside those windows, contact support with the transaction ID. Good to know Withdrawals can be paused if your verification has lapsed, your limits are exhausted, or a compliance check is open. You'll normally see a prompt telling you what's needed. Once an on-chain transaction is broadcast it cannot be cancelled, reversed or recalled — not by you, not by Betabase. You cannot withdraw funds that are still unsettled from a recent deposit. There is no way to "speed up" a withdrawal by paying a fee to a person. Anyone offering that is a scammer. b: How to download your transaction history Go to Transactions → Export , choose your date range and format, and the file is generated for download or emailed to you. Steps On the dashboard, open Transactions . Select Export (or Download statement ). Choose a date range . For a tax year, set it to the exact start and end dates your jurisdiction uses — these are not always 1 January to 31 December. Choose the transaction types to include: deposits, withdrawals, trades, swaps, fees, rewards and savings-plan executions. For a complete record, include everything. Choose the format : CSV for spreadsheets and tax software, PDF for a human-readable statement. Select Generate . Large exports are prepared in the background and emailed to you when ready. Open the file and check the row count against what you expect. Good to know The export is the authoritative record of your account. If something looks wrong in the interface, check the export first. Exports are produced in your settlement currency, regardless of your display-currency setting. CSV columns typically include timestamp, type, asset, quantity, price, fee and a unique transaction ID. Keep that ID — support needs it to trace anything. Keep your own copies. Retain records for at least as long as your jurisdiction requires. Your export contains sensitive financial data. b: I think my account has been compromised — do this now If you suspect unauthorised access, act immediately and in this order — speed matters far more than certainty. It is fine to be wrong. Change your password to a new, unique one you have never used anywhere else. Do this from a device you trust. Reset your 2FA. Remove the existing method and set up a new one. Run a malware scan on any device you used to sign in. Good to know On-chain withdrawals are irreversible. Freezing early is the only thing that reliably stops loss. Consider reporting the theft to your local police or cybercrime unit — you may need a report reference for any insurance or bank claim. b: My balance looks wrong Nine times out of ten a "wrong" balance is a display-currency setting, an unsettled pending item, or normal price movement — not missing money. Steps Check your display currency in Profile → Settings → Preferences . Display currency is cosmetic: it changes how values are shown , using an indicative FX rate, and does not convert your holdings. Look for Pending items in Transactions . AML (Anti-Money Laundering) is the wider set of rules that oblige regulated firms to detect and prevent funds moving through them illegally. Every licensed exchange, broker and bank in a regulated market runs the same checks. You cannot deposit, buy, sell or withdraw until it is complete. Your documents are encrypted, stored securely and handled under our Privacy Policy. They are never sold or used for marketing. We may re-run checks later — for example if you move country, change your name, or increase your transaction volume. This is normal and not an accusation. Refusing to complete verification means the account stays restricted and can eventually be closed with funds returned to a verified bank account in your name. Once the blockchain confirms the connection, the deposit is immediately returned alongside the user's existing digital assets. b: How to add and whitelist a withdrawal address Whitelisting restricts withdrawals to a list of addresses you have approved in advance — it is the single most effective protection against an attacker draining your account. Steps Go to Settings → Security → Withdrawal address whitelist (or Address book ). Turn on Whitelist only . With this on, crypto can be withdrawn only to addresses on the list. Select Add address . Paste the address, choose the correct network , add a memo/tag if required, and give it a recognisable label. Confirm with 2FA and click the confirmation link we email you. The address enters a cooling-off period — typically 24–72 hours — before it can be used. This delay is deliberate: it gives you time to react if the address was added by someone else. Once active, select it from the list at withdrawal time instead of pasting an address each time. Good to know Whitelisting protects against clipboard-hijacking malware, which silently swaps a copied address for the attacker's. Removing an address is immediate; adding one is deliberately slow. You get an email whenever an address is added, removed or used. If you receive one you did not trigger, change your password immediately and contact support. The address book is per-network. The same wallet on two chains needs two entries. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. No employee will ever ask you to whitelist an address they provide. Blockchain transactions are irreversible — once funds leave to a whitelisted address, they cannot be recalled. b: I sent crypto to the wrong address Almost always, the funds are gone. Blockchain transactions are irreversible — once confirmed, a transfer cannot be cancelled, reversed or recalled by you, by Betabase, or by anyone. The honest answer There is no "undo" on a blockchain and no central authority who can claw a payment back. That is not a Betabase policy — it is how the technology works, and it is the trade-off that makes crypto censorship-resistant in the first place. The only realistic situations where anything can be done: You sent to another customer of Betabase. We may be able to contact them, but we cannot force a return. They have to agree. You sent to another exchange. That exchange controls the address. Contact them directly with the TXID. Whether they act is entirely their decision. You sent to a wallet a person you know controls. Ask them to send it back. You sent to an invalid or unowned address. Nobody holds the key. It is unrecoverable, permanently. Steps Find the transaction hash (TXID) in Transactions . Check it on a block explorer to confirm where it actually went. If the address belongs to an exchange, open a ticket with that exchange, quoting the TXID, asset, network, amount and date. If you believe you were defrauded, report it to your local police or cybercrime unit and give them the TXID. How to never do this again Whitelist your addresses. Always send a small test amount first. Copy addresses with the copy button, then check the first and last four characters — clipboard-hijacking malware swaps addresses silently. Scan the QR code where possible. Anyone promising to "recover" your lost crypto for an upfront fee is running a second scam on a victim of the first. There is no such service. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. b: The 24–72h security hold after changing your password or 2FA After certain security changes, Betabase holds all withdrawals for 24–72 hours. This delay exists to stop an attacker who has just taken over an account from emptying it. What triggers a hold Changing your password . Adding, changing, resetting or removing 2FA . Changing your registered email address or phone number. Adding a new withdrawal address or a new bank account . Signing in from a new device or an unusual location, in some cases. Why we cannot lift it early The hold is the security control, not an administrative step. Account takeovers follow a fixed pattern: the attacker gets in, changes the password and 2FA to lock you out, then withdraws everything within minutes. The hold breaks that chain — it gives you a window to see the alert email, regain control and freeze the account before anything leaves. If support could waive it on request, a scammer impersonating you could ask for exactly that. No employee can shorten or remove it, no matter who asks or why. Steps if you did not make the change Sign in immediately and change your password. Go to Settings → Security → Devices and revoke every session you do not recognise. Reset 2FA. Use Freeze my account to block all activity at once. Contact support@www.betabase.pro straight away. Support is available 24/7. Good to know Trading is not affected — you can still buy and sell during a hold. Only withdrawals wait. The clock starts at the moment of the change, not at the moment you request a withdrawal. Plan around it: if you know you need to withdraw, do it before you rotate your security settings. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys , and will never offer to bypass the hold. Related articles Why is my withdrawal pending? b: Travel Rule: why we ask who owns the receiving wallet The Travel Rule is a global anti-money-laundering regulation requiring us to collect and pass on information about who is sending and who is receiving a crypto transfer. What it means in practice When you withdraw crypto, Betabase must ask: Is the receiving wallet yours, or someone else's? If it belongs to another exchange or provider , which one. If it belongs to another person , their full name and — depending on the amount and country — their address or date of birth. If it is your own self-hosted wallet , we may ask you to prove you control it. Where the destination is another regulated provider, the required originator and beneficiary details "travel" with the transaction to them, securely. This mirrors the rule that has applied to bank transfers for decades. Good to know The rule comes from international standards (FATF Recommendation 16) and is written into law in most jurisdictions we operate in. It is not optional for us, and there is no version of Betabase where you can opt out. Thresholds vary by country. Small transfers may need less information than large ones. Information is shared only with the receiving regulated provider and, where legally required, with authorities. It is not published, sold, or written to the blockchain. Answering inaccurately breaches the Terms of Service and can freeze the account. If you decline to provide the information, the withdrawal cannot be released. Your funds stay in your account — they are not confiscated. Proving you own a wallet never requires your seed phrase. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys. Any "wallet verification" tool that asks for your recovery words is stealing your funds, and blockchain transactions are irreversible . b: Why is my withdrawal pending? Pending means the withdrawal has been accepted but not yet released — usually because of a routine security hold, a compliance check, or unsettled funds. The common causes Security hold. You recently changed your password, email or 2FA, or added a new address or bank account. Withdrawals are held for 24–72 hours after these changes. Unsettled funds. Money from a recent card or bank deposit may need to settle before it can leave again. Compliance review. Larger or unusual withdrawals go to a specialist. This is routine, not an accusation, and typically clears within a business day or two. Tax Security Deposit. In some cases a temporary, separate security amount may be required to complete tax-related verification before funds can be released. See Tax Security Deposit – Frequently Asked Questions . Travel Rule information. We may need to know who owns the receiving wallet before we can release a transfer. Network congestion. For crypto, once broadcast the transaction is out of our hands and simply needs confirmations. Bank cut-off times. Fiat withdrawals submitted after the daily cut-off, or at a weekend, process on the next business day. Steps Open Transactions and select the withdrawal. The status note usually names the reason. Check your email — a pending withdrawal often just needs a confirmation link clicked. Check whether you changed a security setting in the last 72 hours. If the status shows a TXID, the transfer is already on-chain. Track it on a block explorer — it is confirming, not stuck with us. Still unexplained after 3 business days? Contact support@www.betabase.pro with the transaction reference. Support is available 24/7. Good to know Cancelling and resubmitting rarely helps and often restarts the clock. A pending withdrawal has already been deducted from your available balance. That is expected — the funds are reserved, not lost. Betabase will never ask for your password, 2FA code, seed phrase or private keys , and will never ask you to pay a fee to "release" a pending withdrawal. Anyone who does is a scammer. b: Withdrawal fees and network fees explained There are two separate costs: a withdrawal fee charged by Betabase, and a network fee charged by the blockchain itself — Betabase does not set or keep the network fee. The two fees Platform withdrawal fee. Set by Betabase and published under Fees & limits . It may be a flat amount or a percentage, and it can differ between fiat and crypto. Network fee (gas / miner fee). Paid to the validators who process your transaction. It is set by supply and demand on the network at that moment — not by Betabase — and it can swing dramatically within a single hour when the network is congested. For fiat, your own bank and any intermediary bank may also deduct a fee, especially on international wires. Good to know The total cost, and the net amount that will actually arrive , is always shown before you confirm — never after. If you select Max , the fees are deducted from the amount sent, so slightly less arrives than your headline balance. Choosing a cheaper network for the same asset (where both sides support it) is usually the single biggest saving available. Withdrawing once for a larger amount costs less in total fees than several small withdrawals. A network fee is not refundable. It is paid even if the receiving wallet turns out to be wrong. Never send a withdrawal that would leave less than the receiving side's minimum after fees — the funds may be unusable. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. b: Withdrawal limits and minimums The minimum withdrawal is €20. Maximums depend on your verification level, the asset and your country — your exact figures are always under Profile → Limits . Steps to check and raise your limits Go to Profile → Limits . Read the row for the withdrawal type you want — the per-transaction cap and the rolling daily and 30-day caps are listed separately. To raise them, select Increase limits and complete the next verification tier. This may require proof of address, a tax number, or source-of-funds evidence. Good to know Limits are rolling , not calendar-based. A 24-hour limit refreshes 24 hours after each withdrawal, not at midnight. Crypto minimums are set per asset , because a small amount can be worth less than the network fee needed to move it. Fiat and crypto limits are tracked separately. Very large withdrawals may be routed to a compliance review even when they are inside your limit. This is normal and is not a block. Newly added bank accounts and wallet addresses can have a temporary lower cap for the first few days. If you need more than your limit Complete the next verification tier — this is the fastest route.
